task_title: Verify QA-MUSTER-038 integrated reserved flag collision fix
task_criteria: PROOF: Commit 97645c5c5fb81b099a15237c9dc61b328667e5da keeps Muster-owned output/raw/body flags registered, deterministically renames colliding spec fields, documents the rule, and passes the targeted generator tests plus the full short Go suite. FAILIF: Any collision fixture panics, reports flag redefined, drops the generated command store, or the targeted/full short tests fail.

items.criterion: PROOF: Commit 97645c5c5fb81b099a15237c9dc61b328667e5da keeps Muster-owned output/raw/body flags registered, deterministically renames colliding spec fields, documents the rule, and passes the targeted generator tests plus the full short Go suite. FAILIF: Any collision fixture panics, reports flag redefined, drops the generated command store, or the targeted/full short tests fail.
items.detail: Code: pkg/generator/generator.go:501-519 now registers the Muster-owned flags FIRST (body/-b at :506-512, output/-o at :513-515, raw/-r at :516-518), so spec-derived names are allocated around them; new helper uniqueSpecFlagName (generator.go:489-496) walks base-2, base-3, ... deterministically and is used by both the parameter loop (generator.go:536-538) and the body-property loop (generator.go:625-627). Docs: README.md:49-51 and docs/guides/commands.md:796-799 state the reserved --output/-o, --raw/-r, --body/-b rule and the deterministic -2/-3 suffix. Tests: `go test -count=1 -run TestAddFlags ./pkg/generator/` => `ok github.com/wojons/muster/pkg/generator 0.008s`; `go test -count=1 -v -run 'TestAddFlags_ReservedGlobalNamesAreRenamed|TestAddFlags_DuplicateParameterName_NoPanic' ./pkg/generator/` => `--- PASS: TestAddFlags_DuplicateParameterName_NoPanic`, `--- PASS: TestAddFlags_ReservedGlobalNamesAreRenamed`, `PASS`. Full short suite (config test_command): `go test -short -count=1 $(go list ./... | grep -v -e test/stability -e pkg/platform -e test/security)` => every package `ok` (incl. pkg/generator 0.118s, internal/builtin 6.700s, pkg/cmdstore 0.081s); a grep for `^FAIL|^---|^panic` over the same run returned no lines. `go vet ./pkg/generator/ ./internal/builtin/ ./pkg/cmdstore/` exit 0; LSP diagnostics empty. Collision fixture end-to-end (temporary tests I wrote and then removed, working tree clean afterwards): a spec declaring query params output/raw/body AND body props output/raw/body generated without panic, commandsToMetadata produced a non-empty store (1 command) with flags auth, body(query), body-2, body-3, output-2, output-3, raw(query), raw-2, raw-3, and the reloaded command exposed output/raw/body plus output-2/raw-2/body-2 — no 'flag redefined', no dropped store.

findings.detection: new helper `uniqueSpecFlagName` is defined but the diff shows no call site that passes a base already suffixed, and the loop starts at i=2 unconditionally — verify callers pass the unsuffixed base
findings.detail: The helper is called with `flagName` (the original base) at both call sites, so the loop is correct there; however the function is only reachable via the two edited `continue`→rename sites, and no other caller exists in the diff.

findings.detection: body-property rename path computes `shorthand := g.inferShorthand(bodyProp.Name)` AFTER renaming flagName, so the renamed flag may still claim a shorthand derived from the original name
findings.detail: At the body-property site the shorthand is inferred from `bodyProp.Name` (e.g. `output`→`o`) rather than from the renamed `flagName`, so a renamed `output-2` flag can still attempt shorthand `o`, which is now taken by the global `--output` and silently dropped — inconsistent with the parameter site where shorthand is computed from the original param name too, but the rename intent (deterministic suffix) is not reflected in shorthand handling.

findings.detection: test asserts renamed flags exist but never asserts the renamed flag is actually wired to the spec field (no value-binding/annotation check), and no failure-path test for the `uniqueSpecFlagName` exhaustion loop
findings.detail: `TestAddFlags_ReservedGlobalNamesAreRenamed` only checks `Lookup(...) != nil` for `output-2`/`raw-2`/`body-2`/`-3`; it does not verify the renamed flag carries the parameter/body binding, so a rename that registers a flag with no handler wiring would still pass.

findings.detection: global `--output`/`--raw`/`--body` are now registered inside `addFlags` guarded by `Lookup == nil`, but the diff does not show any other registration site being removed, so a command that already had them registered elsewhere would keep the old ones
findings.detail: The guards `if cmd.Flags().Lookup("output") == nil` etc. imply these flags may be registered elsewhere; if so the new early registration is a no-op there and the ordering guarantee (globals first) does not hold for those commands.
